title: The Order of Salvation
definition: The Order of Salvation describes the connected biblical truths by which God applies redemption to His people from calling to glory.
summary: The Order of Salvation helps explain the biblical relationships among God's saving acts, from calling to glorification.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the foundation and goal of every saving blessing, from election to glorification.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The order of salvation describes the connected blessings God gives in saving sinners. Scripture speaks of calling, regeneration, faith, justification, adoption, sanctification, perseverance, and glorification as parts of God's saving work.

This doctrine is not meant to turn salvation into a cold chart. It helps believers see that God saves whole people completely, from first awakening to final glory.

Christ is the center of every saving blessing. The order matters because each blessing is received in Him and depends on His finished work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Believers often isolate one part of salvation and lose the larger picture. The order of salvation shows that God does not merely start a work; He carries His people all the way home.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use this doctrine to worship the completeness of salvation, not to win arguments. When counseling or teaching, help people see which part of God's saving work they need to understand more clearly.
